title: Dynamic Buffer for Real-Time Log Streaming
business: High-frequency trading platforms requiring low-latency log ingestion
problem: Standard queues create bottlenecks when logs must be processed in arrival order but occasionally require urgent priority injection at the head or batch trimming from the tail
solution: A Deque (Double-Ended Queue) allows O(1) insertion and removal at both ends, enabling the system to push incoming logs to the tail while allowing high-priority system alerts to be injected directly at the head
steps: Initialize a doubly linked list or circular array to serve as the underlying storage
Implement pushFront and pushBack methods to handle data entry at either boundary
Implement popFront and popBack methods to allow flexible data retrieval
Configure a capacity threshold to prevent memory overflow during traffic spikes
outcome: Improved system responsiveness by decoupling log ingestion from priority event handling without reordering the entire sequence
limitation: Memory fragmentation can occur in array-based implementations during frequent resizing; monitor heap usage to detect performance degradation
